rationale: A wins because it respects the bank-plumbing problem and turns it into usable strategy. Its angle, "Mercury wants to hold consumers' money without being a bank," immediately forces the right proof: partner banks, FDIC pass-through, and legal counterparty. B has real bones, but leading with "The startup bank that grew up after SVB" is exactly the loose wording that gets a fintech pitch killed when the fact block says Mercury is not a chartered bank.
gaps_in_A: "Mercury wants to hold consumers' money without being a bank" is punchy but imprecise; the supplied fact says banking services run through partner banks, so do not imply Mercury itself holds deposits.
"crisis-era winner converting its moment into a bigger ambition" overstates the SVB fact; the update says Mercury became well known after SVB, not that it won measurable crisis-era share.
"Consumer banking will test that claim" is a useful scrutiny frame, but it needs a tighter bridge from consumer launch to profitability mechanics or it becomes a question wearing a headline.
gaps_in_B: "The startup bank" and "profitable startup bank" are unsafe. The update explicitly says banking services are provided through partner banks, not a Mercury bank charter.
"same arrangement that has drawn scrutiny across consumer fintech" imports an outside regulatory peg not supplied in the update. Source it or cut it.
"going downmarket to individuals" is loaded and unsupported; consumers are a new segment, not necessarily downmarket.
"Next step: `meanest-editor`" is the wrong next move for an angle set. The founder needs journalist-fit-check and missing proof, not another roast.
